items.title: Lead Quiet Games with familiar named games
items.normalizedFinding: Begin Quiet Games with familiar formats: I Spy, Charades, Would You Rather, Animal Guessing with yes/no questions, and Alphabet Story. Place optional categories and variations inside each familiar game.
items.expectedBehavior: A tester can choose a familiar game immediately and then use optional suggestions or variations.
items.duplicateMergeRationale: Both notes request I Spy; the second expands the same discoverability and list-organization need.

items.title: Group Mad Libs stories under a Mad Libs submenu
items.normalizedFinding: Collect individual Mad Libs stories beneath one Mad Libs entry and submenu.
items.expectedBehavior: Quiet Games shows one Mad Libs entry that opens the available stories.

items.title: Add a child-appropriate Gross Would You Rather set
items.normalizedFinding: Add a gross-humor Would You Rather variation using absurd bodily or food concepts while excluding crass or inappropriate material.
items.expectedBehavior: Would You Rather offers a clearly labeled, reviewed, child-appropriate gross-humor prompt set.
items.duplicateMergeRationale: Two unique notes independently request a child-appropriate gross-humor category. The newer note expands the desired taxonomy and volume; broader library and interaction requirements are tracked separately in KPF-0011 and KPF-0012.

items.title: Add Race Like an Animal as an active game
items.normalizedFinding: Add a race in which participants choose an animal and imitate its movement. Suggested animals include kangaroo, cheetah, rabbit, and frog.
items.expectedBehavior: The activity explains animal selection, a safe race area, and animal-style movement.

items.title: Add Indoor Marco Polo with pillows
items.normalizedFinding: Add an indoor Marco Polo activity that incorporates pillows.
items.expectedBehavior: The activity supplies ready-to-use setup and play instructions and is safety-reviewed before activation.
items.safetyRedesign: Eyes remain open; players walk only; the adult supervises as a stationary caller. Pillows are flat boundary/island markers only, never thrown, used for face covering, piled, or jumped on. Setup clears stairs, furniture edges, cords, pets, and fragile objects, and play stops if it becomes chaotic.

items.title: Minimize and compact the home screen
items.normalizedFinding: Keep KinPlay at the upper-left, place a concise one-line descriptor beside it, remove the What fits now instructional section, and move the six-category grid upward. Defer richer graphics and animated characters to later development.
items.expectedBehavior: The first screen presents identity, purpose, and category choices with minimal copy and no unnecessary vertical gap.
items.latestObservation: 0.5.0 feedback says Home still contains unnecessary copy and text-heavy controls, so the compact-home acceptance criterion needs revision.

items.title: Show suitable-place cues on category cards
items.normalizedFinding: Replace each category card’s game count with a concise list of suitable play locations, including waiting-room cues for quiet activities and backyard or living-room cues for high-energy activities.
items.expectedBehavior: A parent can choose a category from the current setting without interpreting an inventory count.

items.title: Label Quality Time activities by group suitability
items.normalizedFinding: Mark the Quality Time category and each activity as intended for one-on-one play, group play, or both.
items.expectedBehavior: A parent can identify participant fit before opening or starting an activity.
items.latestObservation: 0.5.0 feedback broadens participant-suitability labels to game cards generally and requests right-aligned compact descriptors.

items.title: Include activities as well as games
items.normalizedFinding: Treat suitable activities as first-class content alongside games, including drawing, coloring, and painting.
items.expectedBehavior: Discovery and category language accommodate both games and activities that support family engagement and children’s creativity.
items.latestObservation: 0.5.0 feedback reinforces games-and-activities terminology through the requested “All games and activities” navigation label.

items.title: Make low-cognitive-load parent support a product requirement
items.normalizedFinding: KinPlay should supply ready-to-use inspiration, choices, and facilitation so an exhausted or overwhelmed parent does not have to invent the activity. The intended outcome is family interaction, closeness, and children’s creativity and imagination.
items.expectedBehavior: Core flows provide immediately usable choices and guidance while minimizing decisions, setup work, and creative effort required from the parent.

items.title: Add a full-screen Would You Rather play mode
items.normalizedFinding: Start Would You Rather in a distraction-minimized full-screen play space with four category choices. After selection, animate one prompt into view within about two seconds, keep it visible until a tap advances, fade between prompts, and provide a persistent exit control to the category screen.
items.expectedBehavior: A family can start, advance, and exit a readable prompt session with one-tap progression and no unnecessary controls.
items.implementationEvidence: Would You Rather now opens a dedicated distraction-minimized full-screen route with four ordered category choices, a 450 ms prompt fade, tap-only advancement, a persistent Exit control back to the originating category, and child-handoff lock integration.

items.title: Build a reviewed four-category Would You Rather library
items.normalizedFinding: Provide 80 original or properly licensed, refined prompts in each of four categories: Cute & Silly, Animals, Gross, and Super Gross. Present prompts in randomized order while remembering recent presentations to reduce repetition. Keep all content child-appropriate; Gross may be odd or awkward, while Super Gross may use mild bodily humor without crass or crude material.
items.expectedBehavior: Each category contains 80 distinct reviewed prompts, randomization avoids obvious repeats, and sourcing records confirm that shipped text is original or licensed rather than copied from curated collections.
items.implementationEvidence: The shipped local library contains exactly 80 approved original prompts in each of Cute & Silly, Animals, Gross, and Super Gross; schema/parser, provenance hashes, child-safety review, duplicate checks, and persisted per-category shuffled bags prevent repeats within a cycle and across restoration boundaries.

items.title: Separate active and archived feedback notes
items.normalizedFinding: Sort active feedback newest-first and move notes that were submitted, transmitted, addressed, or otherwise completed into an archive available from the feedback interface.
items.expectedBehavior: The main feedback list contains current actionable notes in reverse chronological order; archived notes remain accessible without cluttering the active list or being resent unintentionally.
items.implementationEvidence: Feedback now separates newest-first unsent notes from a visible archive of handed-off, addressed, and completed notes; archived notes are excluded from editing, selection, email batches, and bulk deletion of unsent notes.

items.title: Show feedback creation and resolution metadata
items.normalizedFinding: Display each note's creation date and time. For addressed notes, also display the app version in which it was addressed and the address date.
items.expectedBehavior: Active and archived notes expose enough timestamp and version context to determine when they were created and, when applicable, resolved.
items.implementationEvidence: Persisted feedback records now retain creation timestamp, timezone, and creation build; active and archived cards display creation date/time, while addressed records also display the addressing version and date and completed or handed-off records display their lifecycle timestamp.

items.title: Distinguish unsent and since-revision feedback counts
items.normalizedFinding: Show separate counts for notes created since the last email handoff and all notes created since the last app revision. Counters and state transitions must prevent previously submitted notes from being included accidentally in a later batch.
items.expectedBehavior: The tester can distinguish unsent notes from the broader since-revision total, and repeated submissions are avoided through explicit persisted state.
items.implementationEvidence: The feedback UI independently reports unsent notes and notes created in the current version; only unsent selected notes are sendable, and opening the email app does not archive them until the tester explicitly confirms that Send was completed, preventing accidental resend of archived notes.

items.title: Increase color differentiation among interface layers
items.normalizedFinding: Use more distinct colors for the app background, cards, controls, and other components while preserving a coherent palette.
items.expectedBehavior: Major interface layers are easy to distinguish through color and still satisfy text and control contrast requirements across supported themes.
items.implementationEvidence: Forest, Ocean, and Berry themes now use distinct background, surface, surface-variant, primary, secondary-container, and tertiary-container layers; automated palette tests assert readable text/control contrast and measurable background-to-card separation across every supported theme.

items.title: Add settings for timers, durations, and color themes
items.normalizedFinding: Provide a settings area for game timers, activity durations, and app color themes.
items.expectedBehavior: A tester can review and change supported timing and theme preferences from one stable settings destination, with choices persisted across launches.
items.implementationEvidence: A stable Settings destination now offers finite game-timer, activity-duration, and Forest/Ocean/Berry theme choices; each choice is stored under a versioned key, survives recreation and relaunch, and the timer/theme selections are applied to the play and app surfaces.

items.title: Add a deliberate child handoff lock mode
items.normalizedFinding: Provide a visible lock control that requires a three-second hold to lock or unlock and displays hold progress. While active, the mode should prevent accidental in-app navigation or game exit when the device is handed to a young participant.
items.expectedBehavior: Lock state is unmistakable, activation and release require a deliberate hold, progress is visible, and accidental app controls or back navigation are guarded within Android platform limits. System-level escape restrictions require a feasibility and safety review.
items.implementationEvidence: Game and activity play surfaces now expose a visible three-second hold-to-lock/unlock control with progress, lock-state announcement, keyboard and accessibility activation countdown, and an overlay that blocks in-app controls and Back while preserving the recovery control; Android system controls intentionally remain available.
items.latestObservation: Physical-device feedback requires revised lock/key icon states, nonobscuring locked content, tap-triggered guidance, and per-game eligibility.

items.title: Create an original KinPlay launcher icon through Gemini
items.normalizedFinding: Create a clean, minimal KinPlay icon through the required Google Gemini Nano Banana visual process. Explore simple play and curved smile or directional cues, balanced proportions, and teal, emerald, or pale-yellow color directions while maintaining an original identity that does not imitate third-party logos.
items.expectedBehavior: The approved icon is original, recognizable at launcher sizes, technically valid for Android adaptive-icon use, and preserved as an untouched Gemini master with documented derivatives.
items.implementationEvidence: Two original Gemini-generated KinPlay icon masters passed visual QA and are preserved byte-for-byte with provider/model, prompt purpose, SHA-256 hashes, palette, derivative paths, and originality/trademark-review notes; Android adaptive-icon resources ship the approved abstract play/smile emblem.
items.latestObservation: Physical-device icon review found the abstract/cropped letterform unclear. Preserve the approved rounded curves while making at least 80% of K and most of P visibly recognizable.

items.title: Allow selection among supported launcher-icon colors
items.normalizedFinding: Offer a palette of supported colors in settings and apply the selected color to the Android home-screen launcher icon where the platform and launcher permit it.
items.expectedBehavior: The tester can select from a documented finite palette, the chosen predeclared launcher variant is applied reliably, and unsupported launcher behavior is handled without breaking app launch or upgrades.
items.implementationEvidence: Settings offers the finite Teal and Sunshine launcher variants backed by predeclared activity aliases; switching enables the target before disabling the previous alias, persists only successful selections, and restores a launchable fallback on failure, while documenting device-launcher cache and refresh variability.

items.title: Use compact two-column hierarchy on game cards
items.normalizedFinding: Use available width on both sides of the screen. Keep the primary title and content left-aligned while placing compact descriptors in a right-aligned second column or trailing area on the same row.
items.expectedBehavior: Collapsed and expanded game cards use horizontal space efficiently without crowding, clipping, or obscuring primary labels.

items.title: Show a concise description on every collapsed game card
items.normalizedFinding: Every collapsed game card should show the recognizable game name plus one concise description of the activity. Examples include “Guessing game for objects in the room” for I Spy and “Create a wacky story starting each new word with the next letter of the alphabet” for Alphabet Story.
items.expectedBehavior: A tester can understand the core activity without expanding the card, while the collapsed card remains compact.

items.title: Remove negative parent-state framing from user-visible copy
items.normalizedFinding: Do not tell or imply to the user that they are tired or not creative. In I Spy, replace the instruction that references being tired with a neutral “Clues and suggestions” heading followed by the supplied clues.
items.expectedBehavior: All user-visible content offers ready-made help in neutral, supportive language without characterizing the parent negatively.

items.title: Use compact lock and key emoji controls for handoff lock state
items.normalizedFinding: Place a compact circular control at the right side of eligible play screens. Show 🔒 when unlocked and available to lock; after locking, show 🔑 to indicate the three-second unlock action.
items.expectedBehavior: The compact control communicates both current state and the available three-second action, with an accessible text label independent of the emoji.

items.title: Keep locked content clear and show unlock guidance only after a tap
items.normalizedFinding: While handoff lock is active, keep game content clear and visible and remove the persistent locked notification. If the locked screen is tapped, temporarily show “Hold key for 3 seconds to unlock.”
items.expectedBehavior: Lock blocks unintended interaction without obscuring content; guidance appears only in response to an attempted tap and does not become permanent clutter.

items.title: Limit handoff lock to selected child-interaction games
items.normalizedFinding: Show the handoff lock only for activities in which a child is expected to interact with or read from the phone directly, such as Charades and Would You Rather. Most games should not show it.
items.expectedBehavior: Each game has reviewed lock eligibility, and noneligible detail or play screens do not display the lock control.

items.title: Replace the text feedback control with a compact note emoji button
items.normalizedFinding: Replace the text feedback button on game detail surfaces with a tight circular 📝 control.
items.expectedBehavior: The compact control opens the same feedback flow, has an accessible label, and remains easy to identify and tap.

items.title: Default Would You Rather play to landscape orientation
items.normalizedFinding: Would You Rather should enter its play experience in landscape orientation by default.
items.expectedBehavior: Starting Would You Rather presents a stable landscape play surface and returns cleanly to the prior app orientation on exit, subject to Android accessibility and device-rotation review.

items.title: Add a Start action and timed session flow to most game details
items.normalizedFinding: For most games, place a Start action near the top of the detail page and begin an interactive session using the configured default duration.
items.expectedBehavior: Eligible game detail pages clearly separate reading from starting, and Start launches a consistent session using current defaults.

items.title: Add default rounds and per-game duration and round overrides
items.normalizedFinding: Add a default number of rounds to Settings. On each eligible game detail page, allow the tester to choose session duration and number of rounds without silently changing the global defaults.
items.expectedBehavior: Defaults persist across launches, each eligible game can override duration and rounds for the next session, and the applied values are visible before Start.

items.title: Adopt collapsed card, expanded card, and details page as canonical game-view terms
items.normalizedFinding: Use three canonical view names in product records and specifications: collapsed card view, expanded card view, and details page.
items.expectedBehavior: Requirements, tests, and future feedback can refer unambiguously to one of the three game representations.

items.title: Remove safety labels and instructional safety copy from the normal interactive interface
items.normalizedFinding: The tester requests that safety tags, safety references, and safety instructional content not be shown throughout normal end-user play surfaces, while safety remains intrinsic to content design and implementation.
items.expectedBehavior: The interface avoids repetitive safety labeling, but any warning required to prevent foreseeable harm or satisfy legal, platform, or product obligations remains available through a reviewed nonintrusive design.
items.triageNotes: This request must not be implemented as an unconditional global deletion. Review every warning and activity before removing or relocating safety information.

items.title: Remove nonessential descriptive copy from Home and content surfaces
items.normalizedFinding: Remove nonessential statements, including the Home subtitle “Offline parent-led choices for ages 2–8,” and audit the rest of the app for similarly unnecessary explanatory copy.
items.expectedBehavior: Home prioritizes actions and recognizable labels; retained copy has a clear decision, accessibility, legal, or instructional purpose.

items.title: Replace text-heavy Home shortcuts with compact graphical controls
items.normalizedFinding: Use more graphical controls on Home instead of plain text boxes. Remove subtext from every “More ways to start” control and represent Settings with a compact gear icon.
items.expectedBehavior: Home shortcuts are compact, recognizable, accessible, and do not depend on decorative subtext.

items.title: Shorten Home shortcut labels
items.normalizedFinding: Rename “Pick for me” to “Random game” and rename the browse shortcut to “All games and activities.”
items.expectedBehavior: The two shortcut labels are concise, accurately describe their destinations, and remain consistent across Home, navigation, tests, and accessibility labels.

items.title: Add a top-right application menu on Home
items.normalizedFinding: Place a conventional three-line menu control at the upper-right of Home. Its menu should provide Settings, Account, About the app, and Safety and Privacy destinations.
items.expectedBehavior: The menu is accessible, compact, and each listed destination either opens a complete screen or is explicitly staged behind an approved product decision; duplicate Settings entry points are resolved intentionally.
items.triageNotes: The Settings gear request and Settings menu entry may coexist or be consolidated; product navigation review must choose deliberately.

items.title: Fix the Send now feedback crash regression
items.normalizedFinding: On 0.5.0-beta1 (5), tapping “Send now” in Feedback causes Android to report that KinPlay keeps stopping. The tester reports that the same handoff worked in 0.4.0-beta1 (4).
items.expectedBehavior: Tapping “Send now” with a valid feedback selection opens the intended email handoff without crashing, preserves unsent data if handoff cannot start, and handles missing or incompatible email applications safely.
items.implementationEvidence: Application-context email handoff now adds FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK when no Activity exists in the wrapped context chain, safely returns false for runtime launcher failures, preserves unsent notes and Copy fallback behavior, and is covered by Robolectric production-path regressions for wrapped Activity, application context, cyclic wrappers, mailto identity, unsent-only payloads, and launch failure.
